newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Liberal party names Crosby new chief.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Liberal party names Crosby new chief.

text.p: Australia's ruling Liberal Party on Wednesday named Lynton Crosby as its national director, replacing Andrew Robb who quit the position, effective May 2.
Crosby, who has been Robb's deputy for three years, has more than 20 years of political experience with the party, including working as a ministerial adviser.
Liberal national president Tony Staley said Crosby was ideally placed to take up the position having worked on the highly successful 1996 election campaign.
The Liberal party and its junior partner, the National Party, ousted Labor from office on March 2 last year after 13 years of government.
